# package semantic

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-iec61850-model/semantic"
```

Package semantic describes IEC 61850 model elements in engineering terms: quantity (frequency, voltage, active power, temperature, tap position, ...), phase (A, AB, total, ...), reference (line-neutral, line-ground, line-line, DC pole references), energy direction, the quantity a ratio refers to, symmetrical component, harmonic order, the value component an attribute holds (magnitude, angle, counter, state, quality, ...) and a unit hint.

	d, err := semantic.Describe(profile, "MMXU.PNV.phsA.cVal.mag.f")
	// d.Quantity == semantic.QuantityVoltage, d.Phase == semantic.PhaseA,
	// d.Reference == semantic.ReferenceLineNeutral, d.UnitHint.String() == "V"

#### Interpretation, not normative content {#hdr-Interpretation__not_normative_content}

The mapping is OTFabric interpretation layered on top of the normative model; it never changes what the model says. Every descriptor names the [Rule](#type-rule) that produced it, its source and a confidence. Rules are explicit: a data object without a rule is not described, and a rule applies only when the data object has the CDC the rule expects. Nothing is inferred from name fragments.

Data objects whose unit or meaning the standard leaves open are excluded with a reason ([DefaultExclusions](#func-defaultexclusions)) rather than guessed; [Coverage](#func-coverage) reports, per class, which data objects are mapped, excluded or still unmapped.

Users and vendors can add overrides ([Mapper.WithOverrides](#func-mapper-withoverrides)), which take precedence over the default rules and exclusions and are marked as such.

#### Hints and device values {#hdr-Hints_and_device_values}

[Descriptor.UnitHint](#func-descriptor-unithint) is the unit a value is expected in according to the rule. A device's actual unit and scaling come from its configured units (SIUnit, multiplier) and scaling (sVC) attributes; [DeviceUnit](#func-deviceunit) interprets the former through the SIUnitKind and MultiplierKind enumerations of the loaded model.

A descriptor never implies that a device implements the element.

The quantities and phases are protocol-neutral and are meant to move to a shared ontology module later; this package will then adapt to it.

### type CoverageStatus

```go
type CoverageStatus string
```

CoverageStatus says how the rules treat a data object.

```go
const (
	// StatusMapped: a rule (or override) maps the data object and its
	// CDC matches the model.
	StatusMapped CoverageStatus = "mapped"
	// StatusExcluded: the data object is deliberately not mapped; the
	// reason is reported.
	StatusExcluded CoverageStatus = "excluded"
	// StatusUnmapped: a measured value (MV, CMV, WYE, DEL, SEQ, HMV,
	// HWYE, HDEL, HST, SAV or BCR) without a rule, or with a rule
	// whose CDC differs from the model. These are the gaps.
	StatusUnmapped CoverageStatus = "unmapped"
	// StatusNotMeasured: a status, control, setting or description
	// data object without a rule, e.g. Beh, an alarm or a set point.
	StatusNotMeasured CoverageStatus = "not-measured"
)
```

### type Descriptor

```go
type Descriptor struct {
	// Path is the resolved class path, e.g. "MMXU.PNV.phsA.cVal.mag.f".
	Path string `json:"path"`
	// LNClass, DataObject and SubDataObject locate the element. The
	// data object name is the one of the model, without instance
	// number.
	LNClass       string `json:"lnClass"`
	DataObject    string `json:"dataObject"`
	SubDataObject string `json:"subDataObject,omitempty"`
	// CDC is the CDC of the data object.
	CDC string `json:"cdc"`
	// Presence is the presence condition of the data object in the
	// model, e.g. O for optional.
	Presence model.PresenceCondition `json:"presence,omitzero"`
	// Namespace is the namespace that declares the data object.
	Namespace model.NamespaceID `json:"namespace"`

	Quantity  Quantity  `json:"quantity"`
	Phase     Phase     `json:"phase,omitempty"`
	Reference Reference `json:"reference,omitempty"`
	Direction Direction `json:"direction,omitempty"`
	// Of is the quantity a ratio or distortion refers to, e.g. current
	// for a current THD.
	Of Quantity `json:"of,omitempty"`
	// Sequence is the symmetrical component, when the data object names
	// one.
	Sequence Sequence `json:"sequence,omitempty"`
	// Harmonic is the array index of a harmonic value (HMV, HWYE,
	// HDEL), e.g. 3 for phsAHar(3): the harmonic order when the
	// device's numCyc is 1, and 0 for the DC component. Nil when the
	// path has no index.
	Harmonic *int `json:"harmonic,omitempty"`
	// Component is the part of the value the path designates; empty for
	// a data object or sub data object as a whole.
	Component Component `json:"component,omitempty"`
	// UnitHint is the unit the value is expected in: the quantity's
	// unit, degrees for angles, none for quality, time stamps and
	// configuration. It is a hint, not the device's configured unit.
	UnitHint Unit `json:"unitHint,omitzero"`

	// Confidence, Basis, Rule and Source make the mapping auditable.
	Confidence Confidence `json:"confidence"`
	Basis      Basis      `json:"basis"`
	Rule       string     `json:"rule"`
	Source     string     `json:"source"`
	// Notes are remarks, e.g. that an integer value needs scaling.
	Notes []string `json:"notes,omitempty"`

	// Title is the documentation text of the data object, and
	// Description that of the deepest element of the path that has one
	// (attribute, sub data object or the data object itself). Both are
	// empty unless documentation texts were applied to the namespaces,
	// e.g. with official.DefaultDocumented or an NSDoc file.
	Title       string `json:"title,omitempty"`
	Description string `json:"description,omitempty"`
}
```

Descriptor describes the engineering meaning of a data object, sub data object or attribute.

A descriptor states what the standard model and an OTFabric rule say an element represents. It never claims that a device implements the element, and its UnitHint is not the unit a device reports: read the configured units with [DeviceUnit](#func-deviceunit).

#### func Describe

```go
func Describe(l Lookup, ref string) (*Descriptor, error)
```

Describe describes the element a reference designates, using the default rules. The reference may be a class reference ("MMXU.Hz", "MMXU.PNV.phsA.cVal.mag.f") or an instance reference ("LD0/MMXU1.Hz.mag.f\[MX]").

It fails with the resolver's errors when the path is not valid in the model, and with [model.ErrNoMapping](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec61850-model/model#ErrNoMapping) when no rule applies or the rule does not fit the model (wrong CDC, unknown sub data object).

#### func FindMeasurements

```go
func FindMeasurements(l Lookup, lnClass string) ([]*Descriptor, error)
```

FindMeasurements returns the descriptors of every mapped data object of a logical node class, including inherited ones and those of extension classes, in model order. Data objects of WYE, DEL, HWYE and HDEL are expanded into one descriptor per phase, SEQ into one per component and HMV into its harmonic array. Data objects without a rule are skipped, also when the profile cannot resolve them; a mapped data object that cannot be resolved is an error.

#### func FindMeasurementsIn

```go
func FindMeasurementsIn(l Lookup, ns model.NamespaceID, lnClass string) ([]*Descriptor, error)
```

FindMeasurementsIn is like [FindMeasurements](#func-findmeasurements) for the class as namespace ns defines it.

#### func Match

```go
func Match(l Lookup, c Criteria) ([]*Descriptor, error)
```

Match returns the descriptors of every logical node class of the model that satisfy c, ordered by class name, namespace and model order. A class that several namespaces define is searched per definition. Use it to answer "which objects carry phase A line-to-neutral voltage?".

### type Exclusion

```go
type Exclusion struct {
	// LNClass is the logical node class; the exclusion also applies to
	// classes that inherit from it.
	LNClass string `json:"lnClass"`
	// DataObject is the data object name, without instance number.
	DataObject string `json:"dataObject"`
	// Reason says why the data object is not mapped. Required.
	Reason string `json:"reason"`
}
```

Exclusion records that a data object is deliberately not mapped, and why: its unit or meaning is not stated, or it is a statistic or a derived value the vocabulary does not model. An excluded data object fails [Mapper.Describe](#func-mapper-describe) with [model.ErrNoMapping](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec61850-model/model#ErrNoMapping) and the reason, and [Mapper.Coverage](#func-mapper-coverage) reports it as excluded rather than as a gap. An override for the same class and data object takes precedence.

### type Mapper

Mapper applies mapping rules and overrides. It is immutable and safe for concurrent use.

#### func NewMapper

```go
func NewMapper(rules []Rule, overrides []Rule) (*Mapper, error)
```

NewMapper builds a mapper from rules and overrides. Overrides take precedence over rules for the same class and data object; they must name their Source. Two rules (or two overrides) for the same class and data object are rejected, as are incomplete rules, all with [model.ErrInvalidRule](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec61850-model/model#ErrInvalidRule).

```go
type Phase string
```

Phase identifies the phase or phase pair a value belongs to.

```go
const (
	PhaseNone     Phase = ""
	PhaseA        Phase = "A"
	PhaseB        Phase = "B"
	PhaseC        Phase = "C"
	PhaseNeutral  Phase = "N"
	PhaseAB       Phase = "AB"

	PhaseCA       Phase = "CA"
	PhaseNet      Phase = "net"
	PhaseResidual Phase = "residual"
```

Phases. PhaseTotal is a value for all phases together (e.g. total active power); PhaseNet and PhaseResidual are the net sum and the residual of the phase values as WYE defines them.

```go
type Reference string
```

```go
	ReferenceNone           Reference = ""
	ReferenceLineNeutral    Reference = "line-neutral"
	ReferenceLineGround     Reference = "line-ground"
	ReferenceLineLine       Reference = "line-line"
	ReferencePolePole       Reference = "pole-pole"
```

References. The pole references are those of DC circuits (MMDC).

### type Rule

```go
type Rule struct {
	// ID identifies the rule, e.g. "mmxu.ppv".
	ID string `json:"id"`
	// LNClass is the logical node class, or [AnyClass]. A rule for a
	// class also applies to classes that inherit from it.
	LNClass string `json:"lnClass"`
	// DataObject is the data object name, without instance number.
	DataObject string `json:"dataObject"`
	// CDC is the CDC the data object must have. Required.
	CDC string `json:"cdc"`
	// Quantity is the engineering quantity. Required.
	Quantity Quantity `json:"quantity"`
	// Phase is the phase of a single-valued data object, e.g.
	// [PhaseTotal]. It must be empty for WYE and DEL.
	Phase Phase `json:"phase,omitempty"`
	// Reference is the voltage reference, if any.
	Reference Reference `json:"reference,omitempty"`
	// Direction is the energy direction, if the model distinguishes it.
	Direction Direction `json:"direction,omitempty"`
	// Of is the quantity a ratio or distortion refers to, e.g. current
	// for the total harmonic distortion of a current.
	Of Quantity `json:"of,omitempty"`
	// Sequence is the symmetrical component the value holds, if the
	// data object names one.
	Sequence Sequence `json:"sequence,omitempty"`
	// Unit is the unit hint symbol; empty means the quantity's default
	// unit.
	Unit string `json:"unit,omitempty"`
	// Confidence of the mapping. Empty means [ConfidenceHigh] for a
	// class rule and [ConfidenceMedium] for an [AnyClass] rule.
	Confidence Confidence `json:"confidence,omitempty"`
	// Source names who stated the rule, e.g. "otfabric-default" or
	// "vendor:example". Required for overrides.
	Source string `json:"source,omitempty"`
	// Note is an optional remark carried into descriptors.
	Note string `json:"note,omitempty"`
}
```

Rule maps a data object of a logical node class to engineering semantics. Rules are explicit and auditable: a descriptor names the rule that produced it.

A rule applies only when the data object has the CDC the rule expects, so a name reused with a different meaning does not match. For WYE, DEL, HWYE and HDEL data objects the phase comes from the sub data object (phsA, phsAB, phsAHar, ...), and DEL and HDEL imply a line-to-line reference.

#### func DefaultRules

```go
func DefaultRules() []Rule
```

DefaultRules returns the built-in OTFabric rules: the measurement classes of IEC 61850-7-4 (MMXU, MMXN, MMTR and MMTN, MSQI, MHAI and MHAN, MMDC, MMET, MFLW, MENV, MHYD), the supervision classes (SIML, SARC, SPRS, STMP, SVBR, ZBAT, ZAXN), switching and tap-changer positions and counters (XCBR, XSWI, YLTC, ATCC), pumps and fans (KPMP, KFAN), the DER and storage classes of IEC 61850-7-420 (DGEN, DSTO, DBAT, DINV, SBAT, SINV) and the battery charger of IEC TR 61850-90-3 (ZBTC), plus a frequency rule that applies to Hz of CDC MV in any class. Most rules name the abstract class that declares the data object, so they apply to every class that inherits it. The slice is a copy; [DefaultExclusions](#func-defaultexclusions) lists what is deliberately left unmapped.

```go
)
```

Sequences, for values that name the component they hold (e.g. the negative-sequence imbalance of MSQI). The sub data objects c1, c2 and c3 of SEQ carry no sequence: which component they hold is the device's seqT attribute.

### type Unit

```go
type Unit struct {
	// Symbol is the canonical base symbol, e.g. "V", "VAr", "Wh",
	// "ohm", "deg" or "1" for dimensionless values.
	Symbol string `json:"symbol"`
	// Multiplier is the decimal exponent, e.g. 3 for kilo.
	Multiplier int `json:"multiplier,omitempty"`
}
```

Unit is a unit symbol with a decimal multiplier, e.g. {V, 3} for kV.

A Unit returned by [Quantity.DefaultUnit](#func-quantity-defaultunit) or found in [Descriptor.UnitHint](#func-descriptor-unithint) is a hint derived from the model and OTFabric rules. The unit a device actually reports comes from its configured units attribute; read it with [DeviceUnit](#func-deviceunit) and compare with [Quantity.Accepts](#func-quantity-accepts).

#### func DeviceUnit

```go
func DeviceUnit(l EnumerationLookup, siUnit, multiplier int) (Unit, error)
```

DeviceUnit interprets the values of a device's configured units attribute (units.SIUnit and units.multiplier) through the SIUnitKind and MultiplierKind enumerations of the loaded model, so no unit codes are hard-coded. A multiplier of 0 is accepted even when the enumeration lacks it.

Symbols the package does not know are returned verbatim as the literal name.

#### func NormalizeUnit

```go
func NormalizeUnit(s string) (Unit, error)
```

NormalizeUnit parses a unit string such as "kV", "MVAr", "kvar", "kWh", "Hz" or "%" into a canonical [Unit](#type-unit). Prefixes are case-sensitive ("mA" is milliampere, "MA" megaampere). It fails with [model.ErrUnknownUnit](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec61850-model/model#ErrUnknownUnit) for units it does not know rather than guessing.

#### func (Unit) Factor

```go
func (u Unit) Factor() float64
```

Factor returns 10^Multiplier, the factor that converts a value in u to the base unit.

#### func (Unit) IsZero

```go
func (u Unit) IsZero() bool
```

IsZero reports whether no unit is set.

#### func (Unit) String

```go
func (u Unit) String() string
```

String returns the unit with an SI prefix, e.g. "kV", or with an explicit exponent when no prefix exists, e.g. "V·10^4".
